entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Arda of Armenia was the first queen consort of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, serving from 1100 to 1105 alongside her husband King Baldwin I. Born into the noble family of the Bagratuni dynasty, Arda married Baldwin in 1097, shortly after the First Crusade.


This strategic alliance helped secure Armenian support for the Crusader state, which had been established in 1099. Arda's role as queen consort extended beyond her marriage, as she played a key part in maintaining diplomatic relations with neighboring kingdoms and empires.


The legacy of Arda of Armenia can be seen in the Kingdom of Jerusalem's subsequent history, which continued to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between Christian, Muslim, and Armenian forces. Her influence also extended to the Armenian kingdom itself, which remained a significant player in the region's politics and culture for centuries to come.


Despite the passage of time, Arda's significance remains tied to the broader context of the Crusades and the establishment of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, a testament to the enduring power of her legacy in shaping the course of world history.
